title: P/O Stevenson Memorial, St Peter and St Paul Church, Ingoldmells
location_name: St Peter and St Paul Church, High Street, Ingoldmells, Lincolnshire, England
cause_of_loss: Intercepted at 5,000m near Xanten by Ofw Karl Wieland (1/NJG1) at 23:30; shot down (his 1st claim); crashed NW of Xanten
memorial_details: Processional cross inside St Peter and St Paul's Church, Ingoldmells, with an associated plaque to P/O C.J. Stevenson (pilot) of 78 Squadron. Note: the date inscribed on the plaque is 11 September 1942 — one day after the actual date of loss (10 September 1942).

sources.title: Facebook post by Tony Hibberd (admin, RAF Bomber Command Memorials group); photo by Colin Murray; citing Chorley BCL Vol 3, 78 Sqn ORB (F541), Boiten NCA Early Years Pt 3
sources.source_cited: Chorley BCL Vol 3; 78 Sqn ORB (F541); Boiten, T. Nachtjagd Combat Archive Early Years Pt 3

narrative: On 10 September 1942, Halifax DT491 (EY-?) of 78 Squadron, based at RAF Middleton St George, departed at 20:14 on a raid to Düsseldorf. The aircraft was probably intercepted at 5,000 metres near Xanten, Germany, by Oberfeldwebel Karl Wieland of 1/NJG1, who shot it down at 23:30 — his first recorded claim. All seven crew were killed. The aircraft crashed to the north-west of Xanten. P/O C.J. Stevenson, presumably the pilot, is commemorated by a processional cross and plaque inside St Peter and St Paul's Church, Ingoldmells, Lincolnshire, which suggests a local family connection to the village. The date inscribed on the plaque (11 September 1942) is one day after the confirmed date of loss.
community_connection: P/O C.J. Stevenson is commemorated in St Peter and St Paul's Church, Ingoldmells, pointing to a family or local connection to the village. The church chose a processional cross and accompanying plaque as the form of memorial.

crew.name: C.J. Stevenson
crew.fate_detail: Commemorated by processional cross and plaque, St Peter and St Paul's Church, Ingoldmells
